newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NSW Farmers seek complex body in meat reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NSW Farmers seek complex body in meat reform.

text.p: New South Wales Farmers' Association is pressing for an alternative meat industry structure in Australia based on a corporate model with a single board and three subsidiaries, it said in a statement.

Association president Ian Donges said the new body, tentatively named the Livestock and Meat Corp Ltd (LMC), would take over the role of the current statutory body, the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp (AMLC).
LMC functions would include activities such as food safety and crisis management that were common to both the beef and sheepmeats industries.
The organisation would also establish three wholly-owned subsidiary companies, Beef Australia Pty Ltd, Sheepmeats Australia Pty Ltd and Livestock and Meat Research Corp Pty Ltd.
The subsidiaries would have some common board members with the LMC, but have complete autonomy in their respective areas of activity, he said.
Donges said the proposal overcame weakness in both a split-species (between beef and sheepmeat) structure and a multi-species structure.
It could be established without the complete destruction of the current bodies while creating a flexible structure that could evolve a number of different ways as circumstances changed, he said.
The Australian meat industry is presently regulated by three statutory authorities, the AMLC, the Meat Research Corp and the Meat Industry Council.

A report released late last year by the Australian government recommended as a preferred option that the AMLC be replaced with two separate entities, one for beef and one for sheepmeat, and that the three statutory authorities be replaced with two non-statutory authorities.
The Australian government has said it expects to make a final decision on meat sector reform in January.
